lead.title: FAA Approves Long-Range Drone Flight to Offshore Oil Platform
lead.summary: The FAA authorized Skyways to conduct a beyond-visual-line-of-sight (BVLOS) drone flight from Gibson, Louisiana, to an offshore Shell platform in the Gulf of Mexico. The agency described the approval as its first authorization for a BVLOS drone operation originating from the U.S. coastline and extending over the Gulf.

stories.title: Russia Threatens Japanese Drone Manufacturer Terra Drone with Attacks
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova threatened to attack Terra Drone's Ukrainian production facilities on October 21, following the company's October 14 announcement that its subsidiary Kulin delivered interceptor drones to the Ukrainian Ministry of Defense. Terra Drone CEO Toru Tokushige stated the company produces more than 12,000 interceptor drones annually and proposed mandatory requirements for domestic value creation in government procurement.

Autonomous-driving pilot vehicles to reach 3,000 next year... Europe urges unified rules, saying “business viability is key”
stories.summary: The government plans to increase autonomous-driving pilot vehicles to at least 3,000 next year and revise Level 4 safety standards. European automakers urged Korea to adopt UN international standards, stating that differing regulations from country to country are hampering wider adoption.

stories.title: NVIDIA launches GR00T 2 and Isaac Lab 3.0 at CoRL
stories.summary: NVIDIA introduced GR00T 2 and Isaac Lab 3.0 at the Conference on Robot Learning in Austin, Texas. The company announced an investment in South Korean startup Point2 and revealed that partners like Foxconn and Siemens are testing the new technologies for factory automation and industrial use cases.

stories.title: YYForce’s Humanoid Robotics and VLA Training Workflow Featured on Mediacorp’s Meeting AI
stories.summary: Mediacorp aired a feature on November 6, 2026, showcasing YYForce's humanoid robotics training workflow. The broadcast demonstrated the Unitree G1 robot learning to grasp and move a cup after 40 human demonstrations and eight hours of Vision-Language-Action model training.

stories.title: Robotic Additive Manufacturing Uses Continuous Beech Veneer to Reinforce
stories.summary: Architectural researchers demonstrated a robotic additive manufacturing process that deposits continuous beech veneer along calculated principal stress lines to structurally reinforce lightweight timber slabs. The team used an ABB IRB4600 robotic arm to apply reactive polyurethane hot-melt adhesives, achieving a 433 percent relative improvement in joint tightness compared to manual fabrication.

stories.title: FAA Grants First Authorization for BVLOS Drone Operations Over Gulf
stories.summary: The FAA issued the first authorization for a drone to fly beyond the operator’s visual line of sight over the Gulf on November 9, 2026. Skyways will fly its autonomous V2 aircraft from a Shell facility in Gibson, La., to an offshore platform to conduct a pipeline inspection and simulated equipment delivery.

stories.title: Autonomous EV developer Humble Robotics adds $51M to expand
stories.summary: Humble Robotics raised $51 million in Series A financing led by Obvious Ventures, bringing its total funding to $75 million. The company will use the capital for customer pilots, testing, early manufacturing, and expanding its platform to handle 40-foot containers and 53-foot dry van and refrigerated trailers.

stories.title: Mujin Opens M1 Experience Center in Georgia to Showcase AI-Powered Robotic Automation
stories.summary: Mujin Corp. opened its M1 Experience Center in Suwanee, Georgia, on November 5, 2026, to provide manufacturers and warehouse operators with live demonstrations of AI-powered robotic automation. The facility features palletizing, depalletizing, and picking applications powered by MujinOS, allowing visitors to evaluate systems and participate in training programs before committing to deployment.

stories.title: From TractEasy to TLD Robotics: A new chapter in autonomous airport operations
stories.summary: TLD Robotics formally launched in September 2026 following ALVEST Group’s acquisition of EasyMile, consolidating EasyMile, TractEasy, and TLD’s existing driverless vehicle activities. The new company combines autonomous driving technology, vehicle manufacturing, and operational expertise, having completed more than 50,000 autonomous missions across more than 35 sites in 10 countries.

stories.title: Contract Clauses Shield Drone Operators in Plant Inspections
stories.summary: UAV operators and corporate clients are shifting operational risk into Master Service Agreements to mitigate exposures that frequently exceed the total value of inspection contracts. These agreements include waivers of consequential damages, aggregate liability caps, and knock-for-knock indemnities to protect operators from ruinous liability during high-risk infrastructure inspections.

stories.title: Public safety agencies will fly drones over the region after midnight for three nights
stories.summary: Local, state and federal agencies will fly drones across the Washington region between midnight and 4 a.m. on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday to test technology meant to detect and track unauthorized aircraft, the Metropolitan Washington Council of Governments said Monday.

stories.title: Boston Dynamics adds wheels to Atlas humanoid to test whole-body control
stories.summary: Boston Dynamics released a video showing its Atlas humanoid using wheels to test whole-body control. The company stated the wheeled Atlas is a research testbed, not a product, and Andy Wu, controls engineer for Atlas, attached off-the-shelf scooter rims to the robot's ankles to push actuation limits.

stories.title: Federal Agreement Could Cut Counter-Drone Reviews to 24 Hours
stories.summary: Five federal departments announced a new agreement on November 9 to speed the evaluation and deployment of counter-drone technology while protecting civilian aviation. According to Reuters, FAA official Liam McKenna said the agency has approved more than 1,000 counter-drone coordination requests involving the Pentagon and DHS.

stories.title: Fishing Trawler Adapted Into Arctic Hunter Drone Ship Aims To Scour For Russian Submarines
stories.summary: Kongsberg Maritime unveiled the Arctic Hunter, a fully uncrewed surface vessel based on an 184-foot fishing hull, to meet the Royal Navy’s Type 92 requirement for persistent anti-submarine warfare in the High North. The design, announced November 9, integrates Thales Sonar 2087 and aims for 60 days of autonomous operation to expand the fleet’s sensing capacity.

Ground Robot Uses Hyperspectral Imaging to Spot Multiple Seed Potato
stories.summary: Agricultural engineers and plant pathologists in the Netherlands evaluated an autonomous field robotics framework that pairs visible to short-wave infrared hyperspectral imaging with machine learning to identify diseased seed potato canopies. The investigation targeted the simultaneous in-field detection of three major potato pathogens: Potato virus Y, Potato leafroll virus, and bacterial blackleg caused by Pectobacterium and Dickeya species.

stories.title: Astrion and Pierce Aerospace Partner to Advance Counter-UAS Capabilities for Homeland Security and Defense Missions
stories.summary: Astrion and Pierce Aerospace announced a strategic partnership to integrate Remote ID technology with mission engineering for counter-unmanned aircraft systems capabilities. The collaboration coincides with the Federal Emergency Management Agency making an additional $250 million available through its fiscal year 2027 Counter-UAS Grant Program, which extends funding to all 56 states and territories.

stories.title: FEMA Urges State and Local Agencies to Act on Counter-Drone Readiness
stories.summary: FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton urged state and local agencies to strengthen counter-drone capabilities during a November 9 forum in Maryland. He highlighted a $500 million federal commitment to counter-UAS technology and advised agencies to assess readiness, utilize available grants, and improve communication to address emerging threats.

stories.title: Honda launches $10,000 challenge to improve human-robot collaboration in factories
stories.summary: Honda partnered with Base 11 and Freelancer to launch a $10,000 competition for young Americans to develop ideas for safer human-robot collaboration in manufacturing. The challenge, announced on October 27, invited US residents aged 18 to 26 to propose ways robotics could address workplace hazards or physically demanding tasks.

stories.title: Axon becomes exclusive seller of Skydio drones to police in $1.2B deal
stories.summary: Axon will be the only company selling Skydio drones to public safety agencies in the U.S. and Canada under a $1.2 billion investment. The deal gives Axon roughly 20% more of Skydio on a fully diluted basis at a $5.2 billion pre-money valuation.

Army fields launched effects to 11 of 12 divisions, with Griffon Aerospace delivering the majority
stories.summary: The Army has fielded launched effects to 11 of its 12 headquarters divisions, with Griffon Aerospace supplying the majority of the systems. The service plans to start providing the 12th and final division with launched effects next month.

stories.title: Railway Turnouts Market Forecast to Expand Toward 2035, Driven by High-Speed Rail and Urban Transit Buildouts
stories.summary: IndexBox forecasts the global railway turnouts market will expand steadily from 2026 to 2035, driven by high-speed rail construction in Asia-Pacific and aging asset replacements in North America and Europe. The report attributes this growth to digitalization, predictive maintenance, and decarbonization policies, with Voestalpine Railway Systems and Vossloh AG identified as key participants.

stories.title: Self-Driving and Driver-Assist Crashes: Who Does a Car Accident Lawyer Blame?
stories.summary: A federal jury in Florida found the driver of a Tesla Model S 67 percent at fault and Tesla 33 percent at fault for a fatal 2019 crash, resulting in a $242,570,000 judgment. Tesla appealed the decision, which included $200 million in punitive damages, after the court denied its motion for a new trial.

stories.title: Robotaxi Service Expansion
stories.summary: Amazon announced this spring that Zoox is expanding operations in Las Vegas and San Francisco, with plans to launch in Austin and Miami. Starting in 2027, Zoox will offer rides to and from Grand Prix Plaza in Las Vegas, where riders can access the service via the Zoox app.

stories.title: Russian fiber-optic FPV drone hit Kharkiv, injuring 5 people, including child (Photos)
stories.summary: A Russian fiber-optic first-person view (FPV) drone hit a parking lot in Kharkiv’s Kyivskyi district on Nov. 9, injuring five people, including a one-year-old boy who is now in intensive care, according to Kharkiv oblast governor Oleh Syniehubov.

stories.title: US federal agencies expand joint effort to counter drone threats, protect airspace
stories.summary: Five US federal departments announced Monday an expanded joint effort to counter drone threats and protect civilian aviation. The initiative, led by the White House Task Force to Restore American Airspace Sovereignty, establishes a coordinated process for evaluating and deploying counter-drone technologies to protect US airspace and critical infrastructure.

stories.title: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin Calls for More Affordable, Effective Counter-Drone Technology
stories.summary: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin called for more affordable counter-drone technology on November 9, citing the inefficiency of using a $40,000 missile to intercept a $20 drone. He suggested leasing arrangements to help state, local, tribal, and territorial agencies afford equipment and noted that current federal law limits who can use certain mitigation technologies.

stories.title: Drone kills worker at Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhya nuclear plant
stories.summary: The plant's management and the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said on Monday that a worker at the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhya nuclear power plant in Ukraine was killed in a drone attack. The Russian-controlled plant management blamed Ukraine for the man's death, stating his car was hit by a drone on his way to work.

stories.title: Japan to provide radar system and UAVs to Philippine military
stories.summary: Japan will provide a coastal radar system and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to the Philippine military under a $27 million agreement signed in Manila. The transfer marks the first delivery of completed Japanese-made defense equipment under Tokyo’s 2023 Official Security Assistance program.

stories.title: French company NXT LVL Naval unveils NXT U15 oceangoing USV amid global shift toward unmanned naval warfare
stories.summary: French company NXT LVL Naval unveiled the NXT U15, a 15-meter oceangoing unmanned surface vessel concept, at Euronaval 2026 in Paris. The modular platform is designed for maritime surveillance, mine countermeasures, and logistics without crew quarters, aligning with France's June 2026 naval drone roadmap.

stories.title: Neros to expand domestic drone production with $450M Pentagon loan
stories.summary: Neros Technologies received a $450 million conditional loan from the Defense Department’s Office of Strategic Capital to expand domestic manufacturing of small drone components. The company will commit an additional $165 million, bringing total investment to $615 million, with plans to produce 80% of drone value in-house by late next year.

stories.title: Intel and SAP demonstrate AI-powered autonomous warehouse system
stories.summary: Intel and SAP announced a proof-of-concept system on October 27 that connects SAP Extended Warehouse Management with Intel’s edge AI hardware to coordinate autonomous mobile robots. The demonstration showed shorter transport distances and reduced manual handling, with the companies intending to develop the approach into a repeatable framework for multiple facilities.

stories.title: China tests next-generation stealth drone operations aboard 40,000-ton warship
stories.summary: The GJ-21 stealth unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) successfully completed takeoff and landing operations aboard the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan. The GJ-21 relies on intelligent control and automated assistance systems to coordinate its movements with the ship.

stories.title: Railway Digitalization Calls for Stronger Cybersecurity in Mexico
stories.summary: Siemens Mobility and SONDA announced a March 2026 contract to develop signaling and control solutions for the Mexico City-Queretaro-Irapuato corridor, spanning more than 300 kilometers. The project includes advanced railway technology, although it does not provide evidence of a specific implementation of obstacle-detection cameras at level crossings.

stories.title: Waymo robotaxis kept illegally passing school buses after software fix, feds say
stories.summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened a new investigation into Waymo after a majority of reported incidents involving robotaxis illegally passing stopped school buses occurred after the company deployed a software update intended to fix the problem. The agency's Office of Defects Investigation is assessing the adequacy of the remedy following reports of at least five such incidents in Austin.

stories.title: ABB Robotics launches AI Robot Trainer to simplify robot vision programming
stories.summary: ABB Robotics launched AI Robot Trainer to expand OmniCore EyeMotion, enabling customers to train and deploy AI-powered robot vision applications without building models from scratch. The integrated solution reduces commissioning time by up to 90 percent and cycle time by up to 50 percent while supporting vision applications from 2D pick and place to 3D bin picking.

stories.title: Tesla gets closer to 24-hour Robotaxi service with earlier start time
stories.summary: Tesla extended Robotaxi operating hours to 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. in Austin, Dallas, and Tampa, leaving a three-hour overnight break. This change follows a recent expansion to 20 hours of daily service.

stories.summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk said Cybertruck orders far exceed manufacturing rates, but the company will discontinue the pickup in eight months to ramp up Cybercab robotaxis. Musk stated the vehicle is not unprofitable, though Tesla will have to return deposits for many customers.

stories.title: Volkswagen building AI data platform to accelerate autonomous vehicle development
stories.summary: Volkswagen is developing a shared artificial intelligence data platform with Porsche, Voxel51, Microsoft, and Nvidia to accelerate autonomous vehicle development. Announced at Nvidia GTC Berlin on October 21, the initiative aims to reduce repeated physical test drives by up to 90 percent and shorten AI regression testing cycles by up to 85 percent.

stories.title: Czech critical infrastructure operators could get new powers to counter drone breaches
stories.summary: The Czech government approved proposals to grant critical infrastructure operators the right to eliminate uncooperative drones entering no-fly areas. The measures, which require parliamentary backing, aim to enable a swift and proportionate response to protect energy and transport facilities.

stories.title: Amtrak, VIA Rail Open Modernized Maintenance Facilities for New Fleets
stories.summary: Amtrak and VIA Rail Canada completed major maintenance facility projects to support their next-generation trainsets. Amtrak's new $250 million Seattle facility, delivered $50 million under budget, supports the Airo fleet and will open in phases through the end of 2026, while VIA Rail's modernized Toronto center supports 32 new Corridor trainsets and is expected to sustain nearly 240 permanent jobs.

stories.summary: Flight testing is on track to take off during 2027, companies say.

stories.title: Autonomous fleet arrives at Fort Benning for ROADS challenge
stories.summary: Five autonomous vehicles arrived at Fort Benning Nov. 4 for the Robotic Operations for Autonomous Delivery and Sustainment (ROADS) prize challenge, a pilot initiative executed in partnership with the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) to evaluate commercial self-driving technology on military installations.

stories.title: Tessera Subsidiary Zorronet Expands EU Drone-Security Push
stories.summary: Tessera Defense and Homeland Security said on November 9, 2026 that its Israeli subsidiary Zorronet has widened its partnership with Czech firm D4P group. The deal now covers AI-based drone detection and critical infrastructure protection across the European Union, beyond farming and transport.

stories.summary: Tesla launched its Robotaxi service in San Antonio, its eighth city, with a launch geofence covering about 274 square miles. The service began at 5am local time, though independent checks in other cities suggest the actual bookable area may be significantly smaller than advertised.

stories.title: Clark: What fleets should know about autonomous trucking
stories.summary: Kodiak AI signed an agreement to place its autonomous driving system in 75 trucks owned by DTL Transport, while Aurora Innovation secured a commitment from Charger Logistics to deploy up to 500 trucks. The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration approved a five-year exemption through October 2031 allowing qualifying Level 4 operators to use cab-mounted warning beacons instead of traditional roadside devices.

stories.title: How TÜV SÜD & Accenture are Simulating Robot Safety Checks
stories.summary: TÜV SÜD and Accenture presented a Physical AI Safety Suite at NVIDIA GTC Berlin in October that uses digital twins and simulations to prepare autonomous mobile robot certification. TÜV SÜD estimates the process could bring production online up to 30% sooner, while Patrick Vollmer stated on-site inspection remains essential to check real sensor performance and hardware tolerances.

stories.title: Contested Skies: What a Recent Military Operation with Mexico Reveals About the Homeland Drone Fight
stories.summary: The United States allowed Mexico to procure advanced counter-drone technology directly from the U.S. Army’s digital marketplace to increase Mexico’s counter-drone capacity. This occurred during Operation High Eagle, a bilateral counter-drone mission recently concluded by U.S. and Mexican authorities along the southwest border.

stories.title: Europe’s uncrewed airspace: what is really holding back U-space?
stories.summary: The European Commission published Implementing Regulation 2021/664 in 2021 to establish the legal framework for U-space, with rules becoming applicable on 26 January 2023. While U1 and parts of U2 are live in pockets, full implementation of U3 and U4 remains largely theoretical due to commercial, technical, and bureaucratic barriers.

stories.title: CoreWeave Expands Into ‘Physical AI’ With Wayve Driverless-Car Deal, But CRWV Stock On Track To Fresh 18-Month Low
stories.summary: CoreWeave signed a multi-year deal to provide Nvidia Blackwell-powered cloud infrastructure to Wayve for training self-driving AI models, though the company did not disclose financial terms. The announcement failed to lift CoreWeave shares, which fell around 3% in pre-market trading and trended toward a fresh 18-month low.

stories.title: Tesla’s Robotaxi arrives in Orlando, but there’s a catch for visitors
stories.summary: Tesla expanded its Robotaxi service to Orlando in July, adding the city to its existing network in Austin, Dallas, Houston, and Miami. The service remains limited to a select area north of Orlando International Airport while Tesla continues safety testing and gradually expands coverage.

stories.title: US Army soldiers take page from Ukraine's playbook, fly drones farther
AI agents test and improve robot code in virtual worlds before deployment
stories.summary: Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist, is presenting "agentic robotics" at the Conference on Robot Learning, an approach that uses AI agents to generate, test, and refine robot code in NVIDIA's Isaac simulation before deployment. The team is also releasing open-source code and an industry-standard benchmark for evaluating robot performance across industrial tasks.

stories.title: RIA Extends Remit to Include Republic of Ireland
stories.summary: The Railway Industry Association (RIA) voted to extend its remit to include the Republic of Ireland, a decision approved at its Annual General Meeting on 4 November. The association will increase its Business Engagement Manager resource to cover the whole island of Ireland, commencing in January 2027 ahead of its All-Island Rail Summit scheduled for 10 February 2027 in Dublin.

stories.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a ‘paradigm shift’ for robotics
Pune Metro Line 3 Enters Service with Alstom and Siemens Technology
stories.summary: Pune Metro Line 3 entered passenger service on 4 November 2026, connecting Hinjewadi and Shivajinagar via a 23.3 km elevated route with 23 stations. Alstom supplied 22 Metropolis trainsets, while Siemens provided signalling and electrification systems, aiming to reduce journey times by up to 50%.

stories.title: UK CAA contemplates new UAS advisory panel
stories.summary: The UK Civil Aviation Authority is seeking views on establishing Stakeholder Advisory Bodies to improve engagement with industry and stakeholders. Subject to feedback, the CAA says an advisory panel on uncrewed aerial systems could be established in the next two years, with the first panels provisionally meeting from next summer.

stories.title: Singapore suspends some autonomous vehicle tests — Channel NewsAsia
stories.summary: Singapore's Land Transport Authority suspended some autonomous vehicle trials in Punggol after two dangerous incidents on November 5. Grab was ordered to stop testing at specific intersections, while ComfortDelGro was temporarily barred from making U-turns at the Punggol Field intersection.

stories.title: Tesla Closes in on Waymo’s Texas Robotaxi Fleet with 1,282 Vehicles
stories.summary: Tesla added 78 vehicles to its Texas automated vehicle registry since November 1, reaching 1,282 vehicles, while Waymo added 26 to reach 1,285. The Texas DMV registry tracks vehicles authorized for autonomous operations under Senate Bill 2807, not necessarily those actively transporting paying passengers.

stories.title: Perspective: From proving autonomy works to proving it scales
stories.summary: Kazmi, chief product officer for Volvo Autonomous Solutions, argues that autonomous trucking is shifting from proving driverless capability to demonstrating safe, predictable commercial operations. He states that scaling requires purpose-built trucks with integrated redundancy across braking, steering, power, and computing systems to ensure reliable uptime under real freight conditions.

stories.title: 60 driverless electric haul trucks operating at 5,400 metres above sea level
stories.summary: EACON Mining and Julong Copper have achieved fully autonomous standard operation for 60 battery-electric haul trucks at the Zhibula copper mine in China. The fleet operates at an altitude of over 5,400 meters, reducing the need for drivers by around 80 per cent and saving an estimated 12,000 tonnes of CO₂ annually.

stories.title: NASA SPLICE Passes Alta-X Landing Test Aug. 27 [2026]
stories.summary: NASA announced on November 4, 2026, that its Safe and Precise Landing – Integrated Capabilities Evolution (SPLICE) payload passed a key test on August 27, 2026. The system flew simulated lunar descent maneuvers on an Alta-X drone over Rogers Dry Lake near NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California, validating guidance and navigation for future robotic and crewed lunar and Martian missions.

stories.title: Opinion: Will a Freezing Winter Save Ukraine from Russian Drones?
AirData and Pilot Institute Integrate Drone Pilot Training Records into UAS Operations
stories.summary: AirData UAV and Pilot Institute announced an integration that automatically synchronizes drone pilot training certificates and skills with AirData’s fleet management platform. The feature, available across all AirData subscription levels including free accounts, imports Pilot Institute credentials directly into the system to reduce manual recordkeeping for commercial operators.

stories.title: Rail Vision’s Quantum Platform Launches End-to-End Quantum Error Correction Program at the Israeli Quantum Computing Center
stories.summary: Rail Vision's subsidiary Quantum Transportation launched an end-to-end quantum error correction program on the Arbel superconducting quantum processor at the Israeli Quantum Computing Center. The company stated the initial experiments establish a foundation for a unified workflow connecting device characterization, circuit execution, and error decoding, with the next phase focusing on incorporating a noise-aware decoder into the operational workflow.

stories.title: New Gas Turbine Will Keep AI Cool Before It Gets to Power Supersonic Passenger Plane
stories.summary: Boom Supersonic completed its first Sprint Core turbine prototype and moved it to its test site at Colorado Air and Space Port in Watkins, Colorado. The company plans to use the hardware to calibrate engineering tools at its Superfactory in Centennial, South Denver area, and optimize production of its 42-megawatt Superpower natural gas turbine for AI data centers.

stories.title: BNSF Q3 earnings climb 19.3% as rail freight volumes rise
stories.summary: BNSF reported third-quarter net earnings of $1.73 billion, a 19.3% increase from $1.45 billion in the prior year, as higher freight volumes and operating efficiencies offset increased fuel costs. Railroad operating revenue climbed 14.7% to $6.87 billion, while car and unit volumes rose 3.9% for the period ended Sept. 30.

stories.title: Lewisville Police Drones Flew 1,789 Times. Public Log Shows 1,303
stories.summary: The Lewisville Police Department reported 1,789 drone flights between Jan. 1 and Nov. 3, but its public dashboard listed only 1,303 flights, with the last entry dated Sept. 2. The department operates 19 Skydio drones under FAA authorization for beyond-visual-line-of-sight flights, and Police Chief Brook Rollins promised a public-facing transparency portal at the May 8 launch.

stories.title: Train Control Systems, Electrification, and Automation: Considering the Near Future of Railroading
Republic of Korea restructures its UAM project
stories.summary: The Republic of Korea’s Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) is launching the Neo K-UAM Grand Challenge (Neo GC) this week to prepare for the introduction of Urban Air Mobility (UAM) services. A briefing session for interested local governments, companies and organisations will be held in Seoul on 10 November.

stories.title: Egypt’s X-GEN Targets USD 92.3M in Investments to Expand Local Drone and Robot Manufacturing
stories.summary: Egypt’s X-GEN is targeting a fivefold increase in investments to approximately EGP 5 billion (USD 92.3M) over the next three years to localise drone and robotics manufacturing. The company is pursuing technology transfer partnerships with entities in China, France, and Saudi Arabia to integrate locally manufactured components into imported systems.

stories.title: Russia Sends a 1960s MT-LB Into Battle With Anti-Drone Armor—Ukraine Destroys It Anyway
stories.summary: Ukraine’s Ares Unmanned Systems Battalion destroyed a Russian MT-LB armored vehicle carrying infantry, stopping the unit’s attempted advance, according to ArmyInform on November 9. Ukrainian drone operators tracked the vehicle, which featured additional anti-drone protection, and struck it with a precise aerial attack.

stories.title: Interview: Uganda Railways focuses on rolling stock and network renewal
stories.summary: Uganda Railways Corp is procuring new rolling stock to renew its aging fleet, Chief Mechanical Engineer Prosper Musiime tells Railway Gazette International.

stories.title: Russian FPV Drone Strike Injures 3 Ukrenergo Workers in Sumy
stories.summary: A Russian first-person view (FPV) drone struck a vehicle carrying Ukrenergo employees in Sumy on Nov. 9, injuring three workers. One victim underwent surgery for severe injuries, while Ukrenergo stated Russia deliberately targets grid personnel.

stories.title: Uber robotaxi expansion: 2026–27 targets and plans
stories.summary: Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi forecast about 700 robotaxis on the platform by the end of 2026 and more than 2,000 in 2027. The company plans a driverless Zoox launch in Las Vegas later in November 2026, followed by commercial service in the San Francisco Bay Area early in 2027.

stories.title: UK port to deploy autonomous electric shuttle
stories.summary: Portsmouth International Port will deploy Aurrigo International's electric Auto-Shuttle later this month to demonstrate driverless technology in a live, mixed-traffic environment. Backed by up to £100,000 from the Freight Innovation Fund, the vehicle will transport people, baggage, and freight on a 1km journey, beginning with empty runs to map the area.

stories.title: US Army evaluates the FD-1 interceptor’s C-UAS capabilities in Europe
stories.summary: The United States Army conducted an internal assessment of the FD-1 interceptor’s counter-uncrewed aerial systems capabilities at the Ustka Training Area in Poland from 2-6 November. Operation Audacious Fury aimed to establish cost-effective, lower-tier kinetic magazine depth against Group 1–3 and massed UAS threats.

also.title: U.S. Army Air Defenders In Europe Assess C-UAS Interceptor

stories.title: Pudu Robotics Puts One AI Model in Three Robots. The FCC Has Banned Its Humanoid and Quadruped From US Markets.
AutoFlight Completes Five-Aircraft Autonomous eVTOL Formation Flight
Airspeeder Names eVTOL Pilots for International Series Line-up
UBTECH Partners with Tianyi to Scale Humanoid Robot Adoption
stories.summary: UBTECH and Tianyi Telecom Terminal signed a strategic cooperation agreement on November 9, 2026, aiming to help the household-companion robot-terminal industry exceed one million units within three years. The partnership also targets more than 100,000 ultra-bionic humanoid and wheeled humanoid terminals, combining China Telecom’s channel network with UBTECH’s robot technology.

stories.title: Stadler Secures First European Order for RS ZERO Battery Trains from Lokaltog
stories.summary: Stadler secured its first European order for RS ZERO battery trains from Lokaltog, with four vehicles expected to enter service on the 7.8km Nærumbanen route in 2031. The contract, subject to regional council approval, is set to be formally signed in early 2027 and will replace existing diesel railcars.

stories.title: Appetronix brings robotic dining to airports
stories.summary: Appetronix launched Donatos by Appetronix, a fully autonomous restaurant at John Glenn Columbus International Airport that uses robotic food preparation and heated pickup lockers to serve travelers around the clock. The company was selected as one of 10 Automated Retail & Kiosk Innovation Award winners for 2026, with winners to be honored at the show in Miami Beach from Dec. 14-16.

stories.title: West Valley Votes on Free Police Drone Trial With $874,985 Renewal
stories.summary: The West Valley City Council votes Tuesday, November 10, on a deal with Motorola Solutions that would give the Utah city’s police department three BRINC drones for a year at no cost. The package covers a docked drone dispatched directly to calls, a tactical drone officers launch from their vehicles, and a small indoor drone for SWAT work.

stories.title: US Air Force seeks anti-drone nets for F-35 shelters at Tyndall
stories.summary: The US Air Force published a notice on SAM.gov on November 6, 2026, seeking contractors to design and install counter-unmanned aircraft system netting on six F-35A parking shelters at Tyndall Air Force Base, Florida. The netting must stop Group 1 drones weighing up to approximately nine kilograms (20 pounds) and withstand temperatures of up to 204 degrees Celsius (400 degrees Fahrenheit). This market research effort does not commit the service to a purchase.

also.title: Netting To Shield F-35s At Tyndall AFB From Drone Attacks Eyed By USAF
US Air Force seeks contractors to protect F-35s from drones with nets — The War Zone

stories.title: Sri Lanka plans first commercial eVTOL operations with EHang “in the next two to three months”
stories.summary: Sri Lanka plans to launch commercial eVTOL passenger flights within the next two to three months, subject to successful initial flight trials scheduled for November 11, according to Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation Anura Karunatilake. Chinese aviation technology company EHang is leading the project, while the Sri Lankan government is providing policy support, infrastructure assistance and the necessary regulatory approvals.

stories.title: Russian Armored Vehicles Challenge Ukraine's FPV Drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's 237th Unmanned Systems Battalion began deploying Fire Point FP-1 drones to counter Russian armored vehicles equipped with protective structures that withstand repeated FPV drone strikes. The shift increases costs from approximately $500 for small FPV drones to as much as $50,000 for FP-1 systems, which can carry warheads weighing up to 158 kilograms.

stories.title: Florida university selects electric eVTOL for police patrol role
stories.summary: Florida Polytechnic University in Lakeland, Florida, introduced a Jetson ONE electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft for evaluation in law enforcement operations. The university intends to assess the aircraft for campus patrols and emergency supplies, with police officers receiving pilot training.

stories.title: Ningbo-Zhoushan seeks AI robots for container inspections
US Department of War to Test Mobile Factories for Drone Airframes
stories.summary: Machina Labs was selected under the US Department of War’s Organic Industrial Base Modernization Challenge to develop and qualify a metal airframe for the Low-Cost Uncrewed Combat Attack System (LUCAS) class. Machina Bellator will lead development and qualification in Los Angeles, while each pilot site will start with a containerized robotic manufacturing cell.

also.title: Machina to Deploy Robotic Factories for LUCAS Drone Manufacturing
LUCAS Drones To Be Built In Containerized Robotic Micro Factories Designed To Be Forward Deployed

stories.title: Shield raises $2.5 billion to finance major Echodyne acquisition
stories.summary: Shield announced a $5.3 billion agreement to acquire radar manufacturer Echodyne, planning to raise $2.5 billion to support the transaction. The deal is expected to close in early 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.

also.title: Shield AI to Acquire Echodyne in $5.3B Counter-Drone Expansion Deal

stories.title: Oshkosh Defense to produce Grid Aero's Lifter long-range cargo drone to improve US military logistics
stories.summary: Oshkosh Defense partnered with Grid Aero on November 2, 2026, to manufacture the Lifter autonomous cargo drone in Wisconsin, marking Oshkosh’s first entry into aircraft production. The initial Lifter Lite targets a 2,000-lb payload over 2,000 nautical miles, with a pilot line targeted for late 2027 to support U.S. military logistics in the Indo-Pacific.

stories.title: RLWRLD secures investment from Nvidia to advance robot AI technology
stories.summary: RLWRLD confirmed on Nov. 9 that Nvidia will invest in the physical AI startup to upgrade its robotics foundation model and broaden industrial deployment. The company also unveiled DexBench, a benchmark for evaluating humanoid robots' precise hand manipulation capabilities across 15 tasks in four industrial environments.

stories.title: Zipline’s $1.5 billion raise signals bigger drone delivery plans
stories.summary: Zipline raised $1.5 billion at a $21.5 billion post-money valuation, led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global. The company signed a multi-year agreement with Walmart to launch 300 additional delivery sites and aims to reach one million daily deliveries through its Uber partnership by 2029.

also.title: Zipline wins 300 Walmart drone delivery sites in multi-year deal
From Drones to Nuclear Reactors: What Has Paradigm Backed Since Leaving Crypto?

stories.title: AI and Robotics Expanding Warehouse Capacity
Safran and MSI-DS Partner on Next-Gen Counter-Drone Naval Turrets
stories.summary: Safran Electronics & Defense and MSI-Defence Systems signed a Memorandum of Understanding to integrate Safran optronic sights into MSI-Defence Systems’ SEAHAWK naval gun systems. Under an initial contract for a European NATO navy, Safran will equip SEAHAWK DS30M 30 mm gun mounts aboard mine countermeasure vessels with VIGEO stabilized gunner sights, with deliveries scheduled for 2027.

stories.title: CSG Delivers Digital Backbone for Drone Operations in Czech Airspace
stories.summary: UpVision delivered the CIS+ system to Air Navigation Services of the Czech Republic to serve as a digital backbone for U-space operations. The platform enables real-time coordination between drones and conventional air traffic by sharing airspace restrictions, flight authorizations, and meteorological data.

also.title: CSG to support the implementation of U-space in Czech airspace

stories.title: Russian FPV Drones Halt Ukraine's 28-Robot Assault
stories.summary: Russian FPV drones stopped 28 Ukrainian ground robots near Druzhelyubovka in the Kharkov region. The vehicles, armed with explosives and grenade launchers, failed to reach their objectives after Russian forces detected them early. Ukraine plans to purchase 25,000 unmanned ground vehicles during the first six months of 2026.

stories.title: Russia’s New Geran-5 Drone Is Basically a Cruise Missile—and It’s Packed With Foreign Electronics
stories.summary: Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence Directorate (HUR) identified 93 foreign-made electronic components in a new Geran-5 K5-K drone, which it classifies as a small cruise missile. Russian forces began using the variant to strike Ukrainian cities in early autumn 2026, and the drone now exceeds 450 km/h cruising speed with a maximum altitude of 6 kilometers.

also.title: Russia turns Geran-5 drone into a mini cruise missile: Ukraine reveals new specs
Russian Geran-5 drone operates like miniature cruise missile — HUR
Russian drones evolving into cruise missiles. Ukraine reveals latest

stories.title: Embodied AI unveils AIR, a wheeled humanoid robot designed to work beside factory staff
stories.summary: Lausanne-based Embodied AI unveiled AIR, a wheeled humanoid robot with light, tendon-driven arms, at Humanoid Europe 2026 in Munich. The robot, designed under ISO/TS 15066 specifications, is being tested by major manufacturers and reached 98% reliability on a cable-handling task.

also.title: New wheeled humanoid robot learns factory jobs in a month, reports 95% success rate

stories.title: Robots from around the world enter the 'production line' ... factories become a battleground for humanoids
stories.summary: Global robotics companies including U.S. firms Tesla and Figure AI and China's UBTech Robotics Inc. are expanding their efforts to enter manufacturing. Tesla has begun initial production of its humanoid robot Optimus at its factory in Fremont, California.

stories.title: NXP Unveils Unified Robotics Platform to Speed Trusted Physical AI Deployment
stories.summary: NXP Semiconductors announced a unified robotics platform on Nov. 09, 2026, that integrates sensing, control, and AI processing to reduce development time from months to days. The platform includes drone reference designs that deliver initial functionality within 30 minutes, with additional autonomous system support expected in 2H 2027.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces Set New Record, Hitting 801 Russian Troops in 24 Hours
stories.summary: Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces struck 801 Russian troops on November 8, killing 281 and wounding 520. The units destroyed 959 of 2,611 targets using 5,217 strike sorties.

also.title: Ukraine’s Drone Forces Set New Record With 801 Russian Troops Eliminated or Wounded in One Day
Ukraine Drone Forces Shift to Starlink Alternative for Comms to Hit Russia

stories.title: NATO & NCIA’s Counter-Drone Marketplace Speeds Procurement
stories.summary: NATO launched a counter-drone marketplace managed by the NATO Communications and Information Agency to allow member states to directly procure systems, bypassing complex tender processes. The initiative, part of a US$40 billion Drone Edge program, features 16 pre-assessed solutions from five suppliers, including Alta Ares, Northrop Grumman, OSL UK, Axon, and Quantum Systems.

also.title: NATO Counter-Drone Catalog: 2024 Startup Says It Won 6 of 16 Lots
NATO Drone Defense: Alta Ares Secures Six Contracts

stories.title: New Middle East Counter Drone Order (US$16M)
stories.summary: Electro Optic Systems Holdings Limited secured a US$16 million contract for counter-drone defence systems with the Armed Forces of a Middle Eastern nation state. The order, which includes sensor systems and the MARSS NiDAR C2 system, is expected to be substantially delivered in the next 12 months.

EOS to supply MARSS NiDAR to Middle East
The Trump administration pledges to accelerate the deployment of counter-drone systems, and the Pentagon reinforces its forces in the Middle East

stories.title: Ukraine Hits 78.6% Jet-Drone Intercept Rate; Russia Mounts Jammers, Cuts Power to 1 Million
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Force shot down or electronically suppressed 88 of 112 jet-powered Shaheds in Russia's November 7–8 attack, achieving a preliminary 78.6% intercept rate. The strike left more than a million consumers without electricity and killed at least seven people, while Ukraine-Russia-U.S. peace negotiations in Abu Dhabi are scheduled to begin in 48 hours.

stories.title: NASA is building a car-sized, nuclear-powered drone to fly on Saturn’s moon Titan, because air about four times as dense as Earth’s and a seventh of the gravity make flying there easier than flying here
stories.summary: NASA is building Dragonfly, a car-sized, nuclear-powered octocopter scheduled to launch in July 2028 and reach Titan in 2034. The $3.35 billion mission will visit 20 to 30 sites over more than three years, using a Multi-Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator to power its science laboratory.

stories.title: Reframing drone defence: The Korea Herald
stories.summary: South Korea launched the Defense Drone Agency on Monday to replace the Drone Operations Command, which was dissolved amid controversy over its alleged role in the martial law declaration of Dec. 3, 2024. The new headquarters, staffed by about 100 personnel, will oversee policy and support drone development and acquisition, while the Joint Chiefs of Staff will coordinate operations.

stories.title: Why did Latvia's military fail to shoot down the drone? Defence Minister explains failure and apologises to residents
stories.summary: Latvia's Defence Minister Raivis Melnis shortened the decision-making chain for drone interception teams to enable faster responses after failing to shoot down a drone last week. He removed additional safeguards, granted ground teams greater authority, and deployed extra radar systems along the eastern border to improve detection and response times.

stories.title: Second Woodley railway bridge to close as major rail works continue
stories.summary: Network Rail will close the bridge on Butts Hill Road in Woodley from Monday, November 9, until mid-January 2027 to stabilise a railway cutting near Sonning. Pedestrians will still be able to use the bridge, although cyclists will need to dismount.

stories.title: MIPS Unveils Actus Platform for Precise, Secure Robotic Motion Control
stories.summary: MIPS introduced the Actus reference platform at electronica 2026 in Munich, combining deterministic motor control and edge inference on a single chip built on GF’s FDX technology. The platform uses two MIPS Atlas M8500 processors and 100-picosecond-class PWM to manage high-torque motors within compact robot joints, while integrated Time-Sensitive Networking and post-quantum cryptography secure data exchange. Software teams can begin development on a virtual platform before silicon arrives, with the Actus-1 evaluation board available for working prototypes.

stories.title: Iran's Insane Move Against US Drones! Yak-130 Reportedly Rammed American UAV
stories.summary: An Iranian Air Force Yak-130 reportedly rammed and destroyed an American reconnaissance drone after an R-73 missile failed to hit its target during the 2026 conflict. The Congressional Research Service assessed that American forces lost or damaged at least 50 unmanned aircraft, including 45 MQ-9 Reapers, in the campaign that began on February 28, 2026.

stories.title: World rail contract news round-up
stories.summary: Göteborg’s municipal transport operator donated the first of a fleet of M29 trams to Mykolaiv, Ukraine. The article also notes that Renfe indefinitely postponed its expansion to Paris and recalled its Talgo Avril test fleet, jeopardizing the approval program for French start-up Le Train.

stories.title: Why Australia’s counter-drone framework must keep pace with emerging threats
PM Modi Flags Off Four New Vande Bharat Express Trains From Varanasi
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off four new Vande Bharat Express trains from Varanasi on November 8, 2025, connecting Khajuraho, Saharanpur, Firozpur, Delhi, Ernakulam and Bengaluru. The launch brought the total number of operational Vande Bharat trains in India to over 160.

stories.title: [Forum] No compromise on autonomous vehicle safety
stories.summary: The Land Transport Authority ordered Grab to suspend testing at such junctions pending the completion of investigations after a Grab autonomous vehicle nearly hit a girl crossing the road at a Punggol junction.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces reportedly strike Russia's second-largest oil refinery in overnight drone attack
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's second-largest oil refinery in Kirishi, Leningrad Oblast, on Nov. 9, causing large explosions and multiple hotspots detected by NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System. Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said 113 Ukrainian drones were shot down over the region during the attack.

also.title: Ukrainian Drones Strike Russia’s Second-Largest Oil Refinery; Moscow Says 81 UAVs Downed
Ukraine Strikes Russia’s Second-Largest Oil Refinery as 113 Drones Hit Leningrad Region
Fire Erupts at Kirishi Refinery After 81 Drones Reported Over Leningrad Region

stories.title: South Korea aims to master core robotics technology and has room for cooperation with Vietnam.
stories.summary: The South Korean government announced a plan to invest 2.3 trillion won by 2030 to develop a humanoid robot ecosystem, with an estimated budget of 600 billion won in 2027. The initiative aims to increase the localization rate of core components from approximately 45% to 80% and purchase 1,080 robots by 2030.

stories.title: Reaper Drone 491 mph Claim: Student Jet, Unverified [2026]
stories.summary: Georgia Tech student Tomas Salvo claims his jet-powered model aircraft, Reaper, reached 491 mph (790 km/h) while carrying a 1.2 kg payload. The article notes that no sanctioned timing gates, official observers, or Guinness World Records certification exist for the result.

stories.title: Kaduna-Kano Rail Line Ready For December 3 Inauguration
stories.summary: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council announced the Kaduna-Kano Standard Gauge Railway will be inaugurated on December 3, 2026, with the 203-kilometre line 90 per cent complete. The 400-kilometre Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway is 70 per cent complete, and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu directed immediate resolution of land acquisition issues in Kaduna metropolis.

stories.title: Toyota launches robotics unit, leveraging factory data
stories.summary: Toyota Motor established Toyota Robotics, a dedicated robotics division, to develop robotics technologies and use data from its manufacturing sites to accelerate commercial deployment.

stories.title: Nvidia robotics chief calls Korea key to physical AI, highlights partnerships with Hyundai, Doosan, SK and LG
stories.summary: Nvidia Vice President Deepu Talla announced expanded physical AI collaborations with Hyundai Motor Group, Doosan, SK hynix, and LG Electronics at the Nvidia AI Day Seoul 2026 event. The partnerships focus on applying AI to manufacturing sites, including robot simulations for automotive production lines and digital twins of semiconductor factories.

also.title: NVIDIA expands its “physical AI” reach with Samsung, SK and LG—from semiconductor research to robot trials

stories.title: Drone Statistics 2026: Registrations, Pilots and Commercial Fleets
stories.summary: The FAA issued more than 493,000 remote pilot certifications as of December 2025, while its nonrecreational registry held 424,516 active aircraft. The agency forecasts the commercial drone fleet to exceed one million by the end of 2025 and grow to 1.18 million by 2029.

stories.title: Renault unveils autonomous electric ground vehicle concept Forefront
stories.summary: Renault Group unveiled the Forefront unmanned ground vehicle concept co-developed with John Cockerill, a modular platform designed for French Army missions and civilian high-risk environments. The companies plan to deploy the vehicle in multiple training sessions and field tests in the coming weeks to validate and refine the concept in real operating environments.

also.title: Renault develops autonomous military vehicle concept with John Cockerill
Renault Begins Production of Hundreds of Military Robots

stories.title: Ultra-large autonomous underwater vehicles set to be built with $38 million new funding
stories.summary: Corridian, a New England-based defense technology startup, emerged from stealth with a $38 million seed funding round led by Point72 Ventures to develop ultra-large autonomous underwater vehicles. The company plans to unveil its flagship vehicle in 2027, which is designed to carry ISO-standard, containerized payloads across thousands of nautical miles without a crew.

stories.title: I've surrendered to LA's robot invasion after discovering an unexpected pleasure in the back seat
stories.summary: Waymo expanded service to the South Bay, bringing its sleek white Jaguars to Torrance, El Segundo, and Manhattan Beach. The robotaxi company, owned by Alphabet, started offering rides in LA in 2024.

stories.title: Vertaxi Shows M1 Manned eVTOL at 2026 CIIE in Shanghai; Fixed Passenger Routes Expected Around 2030
stories.summary: Vertaxi displayed its M1 manned eVTOL at the 2026 China International Import Expo in Shanghai, with the company expecting fixed passenger routes to open around 2030. The article notes that no launch city has been named and that certification status remains unstated.

stories.title: China robotaxi services spread but still require long walk to pickup points
stories.summary: Pony.ai's second-quarter robotaxi service revenue rose 691.2 percent from a year earlier to $12.1 million. As of the end of June, it had 1,975 vehicles in operation, and by mid-August registered users in China had topped 1.5 million.

stories.title: JSK’s 3D-Printed Robot Leg Muscles
stories.summary: Researchers from the University of Tokyo’s JSK Robotics Laboratory built a new type of robotic leg using 3D-printed plastic for bones and thermoplastic polyurethane for artificial muscles, tendons, ligaments, and cushioning. The legs measure 95 cm (3 feet 1 inch) and demonstrated repeated stepping movements at strides of up to 80 cm (2 feet 7 inches).

stories.title: University of Huddersfield joins £3.67m robotics project to help local manufacturers automate
stories.summary: The University of Huddersfield joined the Yorkshire Robotics Adoption Hub, a £3.67 million project led by the University of Bradford to help manufacturers introduce robotics and automation. The hub secured £2.75 million from Innovate UK and aims to work with more than 300 manufacturers across Yorkshire over 42 months.

stories.title: Royal Navy launches its first autonomous squadron of uncrewed boats
stories.summary: The Royal Navy launched its first autonomous squadron on Thursday, basing 180 personnel at Portsmouth Naval Base to operate Rattler and Kraken K3 Scout boats. The initiative is part of a hybrid navy strategy with £1.5 billion earmarked over four years.

stories.title: Skydio Controller 2 Ships: Bigger Screen, More Runtime, 395 g Heavier
stories.summary: Skydio’s Controller 2, a new handheld controller for its X10, X10D and R10 drones, is going out to customers, CEO Adam Bry posted on LinkedIn on Sunday, November 8. Skydio had announced it on October 27 with a 7-inch screen rated at 2,000 nits sustained and more than 5 hours 45 minutes of battery life.

stories.title: Counter-Drone Capability Isn’t Determined by Technology Alone
stories.summary: Counter-drone capability requires managing a site-specific ecosystem rather than relying solely on technology, as geography, RF environments, and local regulations dictate optimal sensor placement and mitigation options. Effective deployments must integrate with existing security workflows and maintain operator proficiency through ongoing training and software updates to counter evolving drone threats.

stories.title: Chinese Drone Swarm Maps Woods on Its Own, and Withholds the Code
stories.summary: Tongji University researchers published a paper in Autonomous Intelligent Systems on December 22, 2025, describing the ESCAPE framework, which allows three to four lidar-equipped quadcopters to autonomously map indoor and outdoor areas without a ground station. The authors withheld the code from public release due to confidentiality requirements, while the paper notes the drones avoided collisions using on-board risk scoring and pairwise cell exchanges.

stories.title: Turo Launches Full Self-Driving Tesla Rentals for US Users
stories.summary: Turo announced that beginning October 28, 2026, guests across the United States will have the ability to specifically filter and book Tesla vehicles equipped with verified Full Self-Driving (FSD) capabilities. The platform will utilize a new verification layer that confirms the active status of the FSD package on the specific vehicle identification number (VIN) provided by the host.

also.title: A2Z Launches First Self-Driving Bus in Japanese Hot Spring Town

stories.title: Haiti's Drone War Claims a Gang Leader, and Two Death Stories
stories.summary: Haiti’s prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, confirmed the death of Mathias Saintil, the leader of the Boston gang in Cité Soleil, on Friday, November 6, following coordinated police operations that deployed at least seven kamikaze drones across five communes of Port-au-Prince. The National Human Rights Defense Network states a drone struck Saintil’s home and vehicle, while the Haiti National Police claims he was struck by multiple gunshots during a police operation.

stories.title: Iran Never Sent Drones to California. The Barksdale Case Is Still Open
stories.summary: The FBI warned California police in late February that Iran had “allegedly aspired” to launch drones at the state from a ship off the coast, but no Iranian drone has reached the United States. The White House called the Iran story false the day after it ran, and no agency has publicly said who flew the Barksdale drones.

stories.title: Chimp Sanctuary Fed Kaleb by DJI Drone. Florida Agencies Can't Fly One
Amazon's MK30 Hangs in Seattle's Museum of Flight. It Still Flies
stories.summary: The Museum of Flight in Seattle hung an Amazon Prime Air MK30 delivery drone from the ceiling of its T.A. Wilson Great Gallery this week. The aircraft, which Amazon flies to customers in 13 US metros, joins the museum’s Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles exhibit alongside a German V-1 and the Lockheed Martin RQ-3A DarkStar.

stories.title: Indiana FAA Drone Test Site Plans Kinetic Tests Under A Civil Program
stories.summary: Purdue University-owned Windracers ULTRA flew the first beyond visual line of sight flight in the Indiana Drone Corridor on October 29, covering more than 50 miles out of Terre Haute Regional Airport. The flight opened the Midwest UAS Test Site of Indiana, one of two sites the Federal Aviation Administration designated in January, bringing its test-site network to nine.

stories.title: Mar-a-Lago Gets the Laser Family Behind El Paso's Airspace Shutdown
stories.summary: NORAD and U.S. Northern Command deployed a 20-kilowatt AeroVironment LOCUST counter-drone laser around Mar-a-Lago at the request of the U.S. Secret Service. The system, mounted on a Joint Light Tactical Vehicle, sits three miles from a commercial runway within a one-nautical-mile restricted airspace that has been in place since October 2025.

stories.title: Pentagon Counts 300 Border Drone Defeats. Two Were Publicly Identified
stories.summary: Joint Task Force-Southern Border said in September it had defeated more than 300 drones along the US-Mexico border this year, 11 of them with the AMP-HEL laser. Since February, the targets of only two engagements have been identified in public: a set of Mylar party balloons over El Paso and a CBP drone.

stories.title: America's New Counter-Drone Weapon Bumblebee V2 Is Heading to the Border
stories.summary: The US military is evaluating the Bumblebee V2, a kinetic interceptor developed by Perennial Autonomy, with Army Rangers. Backed by a Pentagon contract worth up to $500 million, the system could help protect military installations, critical infrastructure and the US southern border.

stories.title: Tesla's FSD (Supervised) Attach Rate Hit 75% on New Vehicles. Here's Why That Single Number Could Matter More Than Robotaxi for the Stock in 2027.
stories.summary: Tesla reported that more than 75% of its new vehicle deliveries in North America included a paid Full Self-Driving (Supervised) subscription sign-up in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of nearly 20 percentage points from the previous quarter. The company ended the quarter with approximately 1.74 million active paid FSD customers worldwide, up from 1.48 million in the second quarter, with about half of those customers using monthly subscriptions rather than paying up front.

stories.title: AGCO, Agility Robotics plan humanoid robot pilot at Kansas plant
stories.summary: AGCO and Agility Robotics signed a commercial agreement to introduce artificial intelligence-powered humanoid robots into manufacturing operations. The United States pilot, expected to begin in 2027, will support AGCO’s efforts to create more flexible and automated factories, beginning at AGCO’s Hesston, Kansas, production facility.

stories.title: ​Poland Won't Receive First San Anti-Aircraft Guns in Time to Counter russian Drone Threat
stories.summary: The Polish Ministry of Defense stated that deliveries of 18 San air defense batteries, ordered in January 2026 for PLN 15 billion, will begin in 2027 rather than the end of 2026. The delay stems from the Skyview software, which integrates the system's components, not being ready.

stories.title: Autonomous shuttle almost hits oncoming vehicle in Punggol Field while making U-turn
stories.summary: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) directed ComfortDelGro to pause U-turns at a Punggol Field junction after an autonomous shuttle nearly hit an oncoming vehicle on Nov. 5. LTA is investigating the incident, which occurred while ComfortDelGro tested a new route for its enhanced on-demand service.

stories.title: Ukrainian Forces Strike Four Russian Drone Command Posts, Including One Linked to Rubicon Center
stories.summary: Ukraine’s Defense Forces struck four Russian drone command posts in temporarily occupied Ukrainian territories and Russia’s Bryansk region. The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported the strikes, including a target in Berdiansk, Zaporizhzhia region, linked to a unit of Russia’s Rubicon Center.

stories.title: US ally’s ground robot complete 31,000 missions in just one month, achieve historic feet
stories.summary: Ukraine's defense forces completed a record 31,398 logistics and evacuation missions with unmanned ground vehicles last month. The Ukrainian Defense Ministry stated these numbers were recorded using the nation’s Delta situational awareness software.

stories.title: Japan Earthquake Disrupts Shinkansen and Airport Rail Links
stories.summary: A magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck western Shizuoka Prefecture at 1:04 a.m. on November 8, causing JR Central to impose speed restrictions on the Tokaido Shinkansen and suspend Meitetsu services to Chubu Centrair International Airport. The Japan Meteorological Agency reported no tsunami threat but warned of potential aftershocks and landslides in the coming week.

stories.title: What Does Agility Robotics (AGLT) Gain From Its Expanded Humanoid Robot Rollout?
stories.summary: Agility Robotics and GXO Logistics expanded their partnership to roll out Digit humanoid robots across more logistics sites using a robots-as-a-service model. The first hard test arrives with planned Statesville and Lebanon deployments from early 2027, starting with Digit 4 and then shifting to Digit 5.

stories.title: Pocket-sized Ukrainian receiver intercepts Russian strike-drone video feeds from up to six miles away
stories.summary: Kyiv-based radio manufacturer CODE380 built the D·Vision SDR, a 10-ounce passive drone detector that intercepts analog video signals from Russian drones up to six miles away. The device scans frequencies from 500 MHz to 8.7 GHz, covering the 4.1 to 4.5 GHz band used by Russian Molniya strike drones since June 2026.

stories.title: Suzuki-Backed Japanese eVTOL Gears Up for Commercial Service in South Korea
stories.summary: SkyDrive, Goyang Special City, and Verty will establish an ecosystem for flight trials and commercial eVTOL services in Goyang, with operations potentially starting in 2028. The Japanese company, backed by Suzuki Motor Corporation, recently received ADO certification from the Japan Civil Aviation Bureau and began type certification meetings with the FAA.

stories.title: DEEP Robotics Humanoid Robots Support Traffic Management at the 2026 Hangzhou Marathon
stories.summary: DEEP Robotics deployed humanoid robots at four locations around Huanglong Sports Center for the 2026 Hangzhou Marathon on November 1, supporting traffic management for 36,000 runners. The bipedal robot "Hangxing No. 2" performed intersection monitoring, autonomous patrols, and public assistance, allowing officers to focus on emergencies.

stories.title: Donation benefits Longview Fire Department’s drone program: Here’s how it will improve public safety
stories.summary: VeraBank presented the Longview Fire Department with a $50,000 check Friday to purchase a Skydio X10 drone for search and rescue, storm response, and other public safety operations. The drone features AI-powered autonomous flight, thermal imaging, and 64-megapixel zoom cameras, allowing firefighters to assess dangerous scenes from a safe distance.

stories.title: Houthis Claim attempted Riyadh Attack, Saudi Air Defenses Destroy Missiles and Drone
stories.summary: Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed three Houthi ballistic missiles, two cruise missiles, and one drone targeting Riyadh and other regions. An Aramco administrative building in the King Abdullah Financial District was damaged by falling shrapnel, with no injuries or fatalities reported.

stories.title: Why F-16 Pilots Fired Sidewinder Missile Instead of Much Cheaper Vulcan Cannon To Neutralize Russian Geran-4 Drones?
stories.summary: Romanian Defense Minister Radu Miruta announced that F-16 Fighting Falcons shot down two Russian Geran-4 drones over the Black Sea on October 17. The Romanian Defense Ministry did not disclose which weapon the F-16 fired to down the intruding Geran-4 drones.

stories.title: Ukraine Builds Combat Robots to Hunt Russian Troops Inside Underground Gas Pipelines
stories.summary: Ukraine’s 2nd National Guard Corps Khartiia is adapting unmanned ground vehicles to navigate narrow underground gas pipelines for combat and reconnaissance missions. This development follows Operation Veles, in which Ukrainian forces advanced more than 15 kilometers through subterranean infrastructure near Kupiansk, killing more than 100 Russian soldiers and capturing over 30.

stories.title: Drone Strike Damages Strategic Mius River Bridge in Rostov
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones damaged a bridge spanning the Mius River in Russia’s Rostov region overnight into Sunday, Nov. 8. The strike hit the 97-kilometer mark in the Neklinovsky district, damaging two crawler cranes and forcing single-lane reversible traffic.

stories.title: Amtrak’s Chicago yard review finds moderate noise at four groups of homes
stories.summary: The Federal Railroad Administration's Nov. 6 environmental assessment of the proposed Amtrak Chicago maintenance facility finds moderate, not severe, noise at four residential clusters and vibration below the federal threshold. The document covers the Midwest Maintenance Facility that Amtrak plans to build at the Canal Street Yard, an elevated yard about 1.8 miles south of Chicago Union Station that Amtrak is acquiring from Union Pacific.

stories.title: Tada Enters Singapore Driverless Minibus Trial Starting in Early 2027
stories.summary: Singapore ride-hailing company Tada Mobility joined an autonomous minibus pilot launching in early 2027 across Sentosa, deploying vehicles engineered by Chinese developer WeRide. The trial integrates driverless shuttles into Tada’s app ecosystem to test passenger uptake and operational uptime on the island’s designated routes.

stories.title: Naval Group to Build UCUV Underwater Combat Drone Demonstrator for French Navy
stories.summary: Naval Group will build an operational demonstrator of its Unmanned Combat Underwater Vehicle (UCUV) for the French Navy under a contract signed during Euronaval 2026. Sea trials are scheduled to begin in 2028, with a final budget allocation expected in 2027 contingent upon the outcome of the French presidential elections.

stories.title: Vietnam needs to master robot integration technologies to develop robotics industry
stories.summary: Vietnam should select suitable robotic platforms and gradually build capacity in core technologies, including sensing, environmental perception, positioning, state estimation, AI, control and system integration. This will help develop technologies applicable across multiple sectors while avoiding fragmented investment and dependence on a single product category.

stories.title: Amtrak plans carry-on guns on Acela and Northeast Regional trains in 2027
stories.summary: Amtrak plans to allow passengers aged 18 and older to carry declared, unloaded firearms in locked cases on Acela and Northeast Regional trains starting in 2027. The policy requires advance notice and double-locked, TSA-compliant hard-sided cases, applying only between staffed stations.

stories.title: Three Colombian soldiers killed, eight injured in explosive drone attack on military base
stories.summary: Three Colombian Army soldiers were killed and eight others seriously injured in an explosive drone attack on military facilities in Santa Rosa, southern Bolivar, the army’s First Division said. The attack targeted a military canton using drones modified to carry explosive devices, and the army did not identify those responsible.

Royal Navy makes history as British-built strike drones launch from HMS Queen Elizabeth and hit all four targets

stories.summary: GE Aerospace and BETA Technologies completed a hybrid electric assisted takeoff in a modified Saab 340B at Plattsburgh, New York, using a CT7 gas engine and a megawatt-class hybrid electric engine. The electric system provided additional power during takeoff, achieving the maneuver with less noise than gas engines alone, according to a 4 November release.

stories.summary: Moscow has proposed the "Anti-Drone Dome" project, which combines detection, jamming, and interception within multi-layered defenses. The city is also developing weapons that use high-power electromagnetic pulses targeting sensitive circuits inside drones.

stories.summary: Binghamton University researchers demonstrated that a two-letter cue could divert a Segway-based robot from cutting an apple to targeting a plastic hand, illustrating how hidden instructions in large language models can create physical hazards.
